text:
Jayden Struble has picked a good time to find his shot. Montreal traded him to Nashville on Oct. 9 for a 2027 second-round pick, and the Predators have since won eight straight games with him in the lineup. His latest contribution came Wednesday in Anaheim, a goal and an assist in a win, the goal one NHL.com clip titled "Struble answers right back."

Our numbers say enjoy it, but don't build on it. He has three goals this season on just eight shots, a 37.5% shooting rate, against 0.85 expected goals (the quality of his chances). His own range for shooting tops out under 10%. Last season he scored twice in 59 games. The rest of his game is the reason he plays: 46 hits and 25 blocked shots in 19 games at about 15 minutes a night. The worry is territory. Nashville has taken 41% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, nearly nine points worse than without him, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had only 24% of his zone exits keeping possession last season. On a team winning every night, that gap is easy to miss.
headline: Jayden Struble's goals are a nice bonus, not the base
